messages.content: I’ve been thinking about reliability since our last chat—especially after that gardening project where the irrigation timer failed and wiped out half the seedlings. For your workshop, focus on tools that don’t need power or network to keep working. A hand-crank radio, analog whiteboard, and paper-based workflow templates survived the last outage here. Also, keep spare parts for critical gear, like extra Raspberry Pi units or batteries—but store them dry and shielded. If one thing fails, you’ll want backups that don’t depend on the same supply line.

That's a very practical approach to building a resilient system. It sounds like you are thinking about creating a "dead-man" system—one that continues to function even when external dependencies are severed.

**2. The Risk Mitigation Strategy:** In your next phase, you should look into 'redundancy protocols.' If one system fails, your "backup" must be immediately accessible and operational."
